'''Kerstin Heidrun Jordaan''' is a South African mathematician whose research interests  include [[special function]]s and [[orthogonal polynomial]]s.{{r|wisa}} She is a professor in the Department of Decision Sciences at the [[University of South Africa]],{{r|unisa|meet}} the executive director of the South African Mathematics Foundation, and the former president of the [[South African Mathematical Society]].{{r|aims}} She was born and raised in South Africa, Jordaan has lived there throughout her life, apart from periodic research visits to various European countries as a visiting [[Research|researcher]]. She is married and has two adult sons.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Kerstin Jordaan – AIMS South Africa |url=https://aims.ac.za/person/prof-kerstin-jordaan/ |access-date=2025-12-13 |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Going into her university studies, Jordaan considered medicine and psychology before ending up in mathematics.{{r|samf}} After earning a bachelor's degree in mathematics and geography at the  [[University of Pretoria]], Jordaan earned a second bachelor's degree in mathematics education at the [[University of the Witwatersrand]], and became a secondary school mathematics teacher in Pretoria. She earned a master's degree from the University of Pretoria, before taking a break from academia to raise a family. After doing so, she returned to graduate school for a PhD from the University of the Witwatersrand.{{r|up}} Her 2001 dissertation, ''Zeros of general hypergeometric polynomials'', was supervised by [[Kathy Driver]].{{r|mg}}

She was a member of the academic staff at the University of Pretoria until moving to the University of South Africa as a full professor in 2017.{{r|move}} She served as president of the [[South African Mathematical Society]] from 2016 to 2019.{{r|aims}}

==Recognition==
Jordaan is a member of the [[Academy of Science of South Africa]].{{r|assaf}}
Jordaan is a National Research Foundation (NRF) B-rated researcher, recognised internationally for her contributions to mathematics. She has also received a Royal Society Newton Advanced Fellowship for her research on orthogonal polynomials and special functions.  <ref name="UNISA-KJordaan">{{cite web |title=Professor Kerstin Jordaan |url=https://www.unisa.ac.za/sites/corporate/default/Colleges/Economic-and-Management-Sciences/College-Academic-Excellence-Profiles/Professor-Kerstin-Jordaan |publisher=University of South Africa |access-date=14 July 2026}}</ref>
